absent: Allocation and lifetime of open nodes and open files beyond release accounting and counter handling.
Semantics of attribute release callbacks and operation vectors for deactivated entries.
Management of super instance lists and root guard acquisition beyond read assertion.
Sizing initialization and teardown of the global inode hash table and related guards.
Contract of block mapping callbacks and meaning of mapping state markers.
Overall direct IO submission path return values and synchronous waiting integration.
Creation and destruction of the dedicated workqueue used for deferred completion.
Export visibility of helpers that appear without static qualification.
Error codes for stale creation races and unhashed retry termination bounds.
Interaction of pinning with memory management and dirtying policy details.

findings.text: Direct IO staging array capacity is 64 pages per control instance.
Completion option for asynchronous handling has value 1 and completion option for post write invalidation has value 2. They combine as bit markers.

Submission cursor groups block geometry, file position, mapping callback, current page staging, iterator reference, and a head tail queue with byte bounds plus reaping and boundary hints for progressive bio assembly.

Direct IO control groups operation identity, target inode and size snapshot, completion callback and privacy pointer, pinning and dirtying behavior, error accumulation, reference count, pending bio chain, waiter linkage, async context with result, and a trailing union for either page storage or deferred completion work with cache alignment and protected allocation cache.
Release of an open kernfs file requires prior holding of the per node open file mutex pointer and must not use the per file mutex because drain paths could introduce circular waits.
Clearing link counts across super instances requires holding the root super list guard in read mode while iterating supers and performing transient lookups.
Fast hash search asserts opposite expectations about the global hash spin guard depending on a caller flag that declares whether that guard is already held.

New and freeing waits serialize on the per inode spin guard and a bit wait queue, dropping guards while sleeping and revalidating state after wakeup, with freeing wait additionally tolerating hash or RCU guarding.
Direct IO completion state including reference count, pending chain, and waiter linkage is guarded by a dedicated spin guard manipulated under interrupt safe discipline.
Open node derivation, node naming, and hash table scanning rely on read copy update protection with emptiness or root lock predicates governing safe dereference.

Inode discovery distinguishes absent, stably referenced, newly initializing, freeing, and creating cases, waiting for new, rewaiting and rescanning for freeing, signaling stale for creating, and discarding unhashed results with retry.

Open file teardown is idempotent via a released marker that ensures the attribute release callback runs once and the pending release counter of the owning open node decrements accordingly, including deactivated draining cases without dynamic operation lookup.

Direct IO lifetime counts active submissions plus one base reference, wakes a synchronous waiter when draining to one, and on reaching zero completes inline or via workqueue when deferral or mapped page hazards require process context.

Page supply maintains head and tail cursors with byte bounds, refilling from the iterator and on write fault with outstanding mapped blocks substituting a shared zero page while recording the initial fault for later reporting, and discard unpins any remaining queued pages while emptying the queue.
Inode bucket selection mixes the numeric identifier with the superblock address and fixed prime and cache constants through shifts and masking.

Final status prefers accumulated transfer with short read truncation, suppresses faults when progress exists, then falls back through recorded page and IO faults, allows an optional end callback to override, performs post write invalidation after that callback when requested, and for async paths advances position and applies sync before invoking completion and freeing the control.

Synchronous write handling treats either an explicit dsync request or a synchronously flagged target as requiring range synchronization, otherwise optionally kicking writeback avoidance for dontcache requests.
Direct IO exit decrements the per inode direct count and wakes waiters when reaching zero.

Block acquisition forbids creation for hole skipping writes inside current size to permit fallback, records private mapping data for completion, and propagates deferral requests from the mapping layer.

Bio construction selects operation dependent completion, marks pinning, copies write hints, assigns sector offsets and logical ranges, increments references before submission, appends page sections with pin retention and block progression, and periodically reaps completed entries with error propagation while bounding vector counts and pairing pin with unpin on teardown.
Link count clearing walks all super instances of a root and clears counts only where an in memory inode is currently found, ignoring absent entries.
Hashtable lookup by superblock and number provides a referenced stable inode or null, hiding transient creation and freeing races from callers.
Blocking wait for initial inode construction to clear, usable by lookup paths encountering partially initialized entries.
Accessor returning the node that represents a filesystem root.
Early boot selector enabling tmpfs based root handling when no explicit root name exists or when the configured filesystem list mentions tmpfs.
Lookup and wait paths may sleep or schedule while holding only fine grained or RCU guards, requiring sleepable context and retry tolerance for concurrent eviction and hash changes.

Faults during page extraction and per bio failures are deferred and may be superseded by transfer progress or later overrides, with zero substitution potentially masking original memory errors until mapped blocks are consumed.
